items.title: The Killers’ Dave Keuning Reveals He Survived a Life-Threatening Stroke
items.summary:
Dave Keuning, the guitarist who co-founded The Killers, told fans he suffered a major stroke two weeks ago and underwent emergency surgery. He shared the news in an Instagram post on Thanksgiving, as Consequence reported, and said he has recovered.

Keuning described a blood clot that cut off blood supply to the entire right side of his brain. "By the time I arrived at the hospital, I was blind in one eye and had lost function on my left side, but I still wasn't able to realize I was having a stroke," he wrote. Doctors gave him a 40% chance of survival and warned he could be left with lasting disabilities.

"But by some miracle I am fine," Keuning said, telling fans he can play guitar just as well as before. He added that checking whether he could still play was the first thing he did when he woke up from surgery.

"I feel extremely fortunate that I am alive and well, and that I can use my hands and feet and talk just like before," he wrote, thanking his wife, his son, his daughter and his bandmates, who he said he feels closer to than ever.

Keuning started The Killers with Brandon Flowers in 2001 and co-wrote the band's best-known songs, among them "Mr. Brightside," "Somebody Told Me" and "When You Were Young." He stepped away from the group in 2017, pointing to the demands of its touring schedule, and returned to record 2021's Pressure Machine.

items.title: Watch Goo Goo Dolls’ Complete NFL Halftime Show
items.summary:
The Buffalo Bills posted the Goo Goo Dolls' full Thanksgiving halftime performance online after NBC aired roughly 30 seconds of it during the network's broadcast of the Bills' game against the Kansas City Chiefs. The set ran more than 10 minutes at Highmark Stadium in Buffalo, with the band playing "Iris," "Broadway" and "Slide" in the rain.

Rather than carry the performance, NBC stayed with studio conversation between Mike Tirico and Mike Tomlin about Aaron Rodgers, a choice that drew immediate complaints from viewers. Rolling Stone reported that fans at the stadium praised the set, with some calling it one of the best they had seen, while one viewer online wrote, "Aaron Rodgers ruins one last thing as NBC airs Tomlin interview instead of Goo Goo Dolls concert."

Steven Van Zandt weighed in on X, writing of the band, "They are a great band. That was badly handled and disrespectful."

The Goo Goo Dolls were one of three acts booked across the NFL's Thanksgiving slate. Earlier in the day, Wu-Tang Clan performed at Ford Field in Detroit during the Chicago Bears' game against the Lions, opening with "Triumph" from 1997's Wu-Tang Forever with Red Hot Chili Peppers drummer Chad Smith behind the kit. The group ran a medley of "C.R.E.A.M.," "Da Mystery of Chessboxin'" and "Bring Da Ruckus," and Ol' Dirty Bastard's son Young Dirty Bastard handled his father's verses on "Shimmy Shimmy Ya."

Miranda Lambert closed out the day's halftime bookings at AT&T Stadium during the Dallas Cowboys' game against the Philadelphia Eagles, performing "Snakeskin Boots," "Kerosene," "Gunpowder & Lead," "Mama's Broken Heart" and "Little Red Wagon." The Bills' upload leaves the Goo Goo Dolls' performance available in full, outside the broadcast that cut it.

items.title: Doha Winners: ‘A Girl Unknown’ & ‘Concrete Land’ Scoop Top Prizes
items.summary:
Chinese director Zou Jing's A Girl Unknown won the $75,000 Best Narrative prize at the Doha Film Festival, which closed Friday evening after the second edition of its revamped format. The debut feature follows a girl abandoned as a baby in a rubbish bin who grows into adolescence under three different sets of guardians and circumstances.

The film premiered at Cannes Critics' Week earlier this year, where it took the Fipresci Prize. Greenwich Entertainment acquired it for the United States and is planning a tour and release in early 2027.

Rafael Manuel won Best Artistic Achievement in Narrative for Filipiñana, about a 17-year-old girl who uncovers the uglier workings of the upscale country club where she works on the golf course. The film premiered at Sundance, won the World Cinema Special Jury Award there, and is the Philippines' entry for the 99th Academy Awards.

The jury awarded Best Actress posthumously to Josette Kwanya for House of the Wind, directed by her son Auguste Bernard Kouemo, in which she plays an elderly Cameroonian woman waiting for children who left for Europe. The film premiered in Venice's Orizzonti sidebar in September and won the Lion of the Future for a debut. Japanese director Naomi Kawase presided over this year's jury alongside Gianfranco Rosi, Adam Bessa, Dora Bouchoucha and Kamal Aljafari.

Deadline reported that Asmahan Bkerat's Concrete Land, about a Bedouin family trying to maintain a traditional life in tents, took both Best Documentary and the Fipresci prize, handed out at the festival for the first time this year. Tala Hadid's Bardi won Best Artistic Achievement for Documentary.

Festival director and Doha Film Institute CEO Fatma Hassan Alremaihi framed the slate around the institute's belief in "the power of stories to transcend borders, challenge perspectives and bring the experiences of people and communities into the global conversation." She added that the festival exists to champion "bold and independent storytelling, and creating space for stories that might otherwise go untold."
